To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Mg/Ca ratio of Cyprideis is a useful palaeosalinity indicator for the gulf of Australia; (ii) the Sr/Ca ratio of this ostracod is a sensitive indicator of the precipitation of authigenically calcified minerals, and (iii) ostracod shell geochemistry is a useful palæoenvironmental tool in the reconstruction of past hydrological conditions in the Gulf of Carpenaria.

ostracod shells from the Gulf ofCarpentaria record a history of fresh or slightly saline conditions during sea level lowstands, and that ostracod shell Mg/Ca ratios are sensitive to changes in salinity and Sr/Ca and to authigenic calcitic precipitates.

the Mg/Ca ratio in the ostracod Cyproideis from a core taken from the Gulf of Carpentiaria, Australia, can be used to reconstruct the salinity of the water in which the ostracods lived, and that this salinity changed from fresh to slightly saline during the past 13,000 years.

the use of ostracods as a new tool to determine the palaeoenvironments of the Gulf of Carpendaria, Australia, over the past 40 kyr.
the development of a new palaeoenviron- mental indicator for the reconstruction of the chemical changes occurring in a lake environment during marine transgression and regression.
the application of ostracod shell geochemistry to palaeoenvironment studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ostracod Mg/Ca and, to a lesser extent, Sr/Ca ratios can provide a reliable record of the chemical composition of the water in which they were deposited, and thus can be used to infer palaeoenvironment conditions.
the ostracod Mg/Ca and Ca/Ca ratios are good indicators of the salinity of the water, while the Sr/Ca ratio of the water is a good indicator of the carbonate content of the water.
the Mg/Ca ratios in the ostracod shells reflect the salinity of the water, and that the Sr/Ca ratio is sensitive to the Ca depletion of waters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ostracods can be a very useful tool for palaeoenvironment studies in the future, and that the Mg/Ca ratio in the ostracod shells is an excellent indicator of the salinity of the water in which they lived.

1) the ostracod shells record the chemical composition of the lake water during the past 50,000 years; 2) the chemical composition of lake water is controlled by precipitation of authigenetic carbonate and the hydrology of the catchment basin; 3) during sea level lowstands, the lake was fresh or slightly saline and the water was depleted in Sr and Mg.
the Mg/Ca ratio of ostracod shells can be used as a proxy for salinity and that the Sr/Ca ratio of the shell is a good indicator of authigenic mineral precipitation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ostracods can be used to determine past water chemistry, and that the Mg/Ca ratio of the water can be used to infer the degree of salinity in a water body.

ostracod shell Mg/Ca and Ca/Sr can be used to monitor the changes in salinity and Ca concentration of the water during transgressive/regressive cycles, and that ostracods can be used to determine the duration and timing of such cycles in the past.
ostracod shell Mg/Ca and, especially, Sr/Ca ratios can be successfully used to reconstruct palaeoenvironment changes in the gulf.
